# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll explore the codebase to find the transaction labeling logic and the edge-case faults described in the forum digest.

# Codebase exploration: transaction labeling

## Project structure overview

This is a **Flask microservice** (`transaction-enrichment-python`) that categorizes Indian bank statement rows via regex/rule engines.

```
/app
├── Dockerfile                          # gunicorn on :9898
├── .gitignore
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # Flask, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, scipy/sklearn
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app bootstrap
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP API + per-bank pipeline orchestration
        ├── BankScripts/                # 35 bank-specific parsers
        │   ├── HDFC.py, ICICI.py, SBI.py, Axis.py, Kotak.py, PNB.py, ...
        └── UtilityScripts/             # Shared post-processing
            ├── AppUtil.py              # DF clean + sep_by_*/py_extract helpers
            ├── RegexConstants.py       # Cross-bank purpose/merchant regexes
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py   # Bank-specific narration patterns
            ├── Purpose.py              # transactionSubcategory + merchantType
            ├── CleanName.py            # Merchant name normalization (~2k lines)
            ├── SalaryDetection.py      # Clustering-based salary inference
            ├── InternalPayment.py      # Self-transfer detection
            ├── PFMCategorization.py    # PFM L1/L2 categories
            ├── SimpleDescription.py    # Human-readable PFM description
            ├── CardPurpose.py / CardCleanNames.py
            ├── RecurrentTxns.py
            └── *Enums.py               # Category/subcategory display names
```

**No test suite exists** (no `tests/`, no `pytest`, no sample fixtures). Only a single git commit: `import codebase`.

---

## How labeling works

### API entry

`POST /categorizeTransaction` in `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`

Payload fields: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]`.

### Pipeline (same order for every bank)

1. `AppUtil.clean_input_df` — strip description, numeric amount/balance  
2. **Bank script** `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(df, accountType)`  
   - Sets `transactionCategory` (default often `"TRANSFER"`)  
   - May set initial `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`  
   - Extracts **`partyName`** (counterparty/payee) from narration via `/`, `-`, `*`, `:`, regex  
   - Builds `party2` = space-stripped `partyName` for matching  
3. Credit cards: `card_clean_names` → `card_purpose`  
4. **`purpose(df, accountType)`** — broad subcategory + merchantType rules  
5. **`clean_names(df, accountType, bank)`** — brand/merchant canonicalization into `partyName`  
6. **`internal_payment`** (if holder name present) — fuzzy match → `INTERNAL_PAYMENT`  
7. **`salary_detection`** (SAVING only) — hierarchical clustering on party names  
8. If PFM: `pfm_categorization` → `simple_description`

### Output fields (label map)

| Conceptual label | Code field |
|---|---|
| Category | `transactionCategory` |
| Sub-category / purpose | `transactionSubcategory` |
| Sub-tag / merchant type | `merchantType` |
| Payee / counterparty | `partyName` (`party2` = normalized) |
| PFM | `pfmCategoryOne`, `pfmCategoryTwo`, `pfmCategoryType`, `pfmSimpleDescription` |
| Internal flag | `isInternalPayment` |

### Rule-engine mechanics

Almost everything is **ordered `np.select(conditions, choices)`** — first matching condition wins. Helpers in `AppUtil.py`:

- `sep_by_(desc, n1, n2)` — slash segments joined  
- `sep_by_dash` / `sep_by_star` / `sep_by_colon` / etc.  
- `py_extract(desc, pat, index)` — regex capture  

---

## Key files and roles

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `Controller.py` | Routes; bank switch; pipeline order |
| `BankScripts/*.py` | Narration → category + first-pass `partyName` |
| `Purpose.py` | Cross-bank subcategory (SALARY, LOAN, bounce types…) + merchantType |
| `CleanName.py` | Maps party/description → clean brand names (DTH, utilities, apps…) |
| `RegexConstants.py` | SALARY, LOAN, TECHNICAL_BOUNCE, INSUFF_BOUNCE, merchant lists |
| `BankRegexConstants.py` | HDFC cheque/FT patterns, Kotak FT/CHQ/TO patterns, PNB TO/FROM, SBI IMPS… |
| `SalaryDetection.py` | Frequency/amount/party clustering for SALARY vs REIMBURSEMENT |
| `InternalPayment.py` | Fuzzy match party vs account holder |
| `PFMCategorization.py` | Maps internal cats → PFM expense/income/transfer tree |
| `SimpleDescription.py` | `partyName` or `partyName - Category` display string |
| `*Enums.py` | Human labels only (not used in matching) |

---

## The five bug areas — code locations

### 1. Cheque deposits / numeric reference credits / transfers

**Category assignment (cheque):**

- **HDFC** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py`  
  - L69–75: CHQ keywords → `CHEQUE_RETURN` / `CHEQUE_PAID` / `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`  
  - **L100**: bare numeric remark as cheque:  
    `remark len==15` and `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` → `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`  
  - Risk: numeric refs that are not cheques can be mislabeled; order vs other rules matters  
- **Axis** L58–59: `remark ^[0-9]{5,6}$` → CHEQUE_PAID/DEPOSIT by type  
- **PNB** L60–61, **YES** L53, **UCO** L45: same 3–6 digit remark → cheque  
- **IDBI** L57–58: pure alpha description CREDIT → CHEQUE_DEPOSIT (aggressive)  
- **IDFC** L42: `cheque|CHQ DEP/` CREDIT → CHEQUE_DEPOSIT  

**Party extraction for cheques:**

- HDFC L188: `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1` + colon split  
- Patterns in `BankRegexConstants.py` L80–90 (`HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN*`)  
- Kotak L230–241: `CLG TO` / `TO CLG` / `CHQ_PATTERN*`  
- PNB L122–131: `PNB_CHQ_0`…`PNB_CHQ_8` (`^TO TRF`, `^TO `, etc.)  
- Axis L149–150: CHEQUE with plain description as partyName  

**Likely bugs:**

- Numeric-only remarks/descriptions treated as cheque when they may be transfers or salary refs  
- HDFC L261 blanks partyName if no letters — numeric cheque payees wiped  
- Default category `"TRANSFER"` when no pattern matches → numeric credits become TRANSFER then may hit salary rules  

---

### 2. Salary credits with bare numeric codes

**Bank-level:**

```124:124:/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py
[transactions.transactionCategory.eq("TRANSFER") & transactions.description.str.contains("^[0-9]{6}$", ...) & type.eq("CREDIT") & (accountType=="SAVINGS") , "SALARY"],
```

**Confirmed bug:** Controller and all other banks use `accountType == "SAVING"`, but HDFC checks **`"SAVINGS"`**. This bare-6-digit salary rule **never fires** in production.

Other salary hooks:

- HDFC L119: `^A2AINT01` → SALARY  
- ICICI L105: `^ICSP/` + SAVING → SALARY  
- ICICI L113: `INF/INFT` + salary keywords  
- Axis L99: `TRANSFER/TB/25-|BRN-SALARY PAYMENT-|MBSALARY|...`  
- SBI L84: `\bSAL[0-9]+` CREDIT → SALARY  
- `Purpose.py` L13–17: `SALARY` / `salary` / `SAL_IMPS` regexes from `RegexConstants.py` L6–7  
- `SalaryDetection.py`: clustering; **requires non-empty `partyName`** (L50) — bare numeric codes with empty party never enter salary detection  

**Likely bugs:**

- HDFC `SAVINGS` vs `SAVING` typo  
- Bare codes → empty partyName → salary_detection skips them  
- Over-broad Purpose salary keywords (`Advance`, month names) can false-positive  

---

### 3. Transfers with direction words ahead of names

**Strip TO/FROM/TRF prefixes after extraction:**

| Location | Pattern |
|---|---|
| HDFC L253–257 | `^By `, `Trf To`, `Fnf To`, `Paid To`, `Fund Trf To`, `^Trf ` |
| Axis L167, L181 | `^TRANSFER TO `, `^Trf From ` |
| ICICI L201–203, L231–232 | IMPS ` To `, `^To `, `^Trfto ` |
| SBI L181 | `Transfer To\|Transfer From\|...` via `TRF_STOP_WORDS` |
| UnionBank L118–121 | `^TRF? TO `, `^TO TR `, `^TO [A-Z]` |
| PNB | `PNB_TRF_1/2` = `^FROM (.*)`, cheque `^TO TRF` etc. |
| Kotak | Large `FT_PATTERN*` / `FT_CHQ_PATTERN*` in BankRegexConstants L241–298 |

**Shared stop-words** (`BankRegexConstants.py` L65):

```text
TRF_STOP_WORDS = "^By Transfer.*|Transfer To.*|^To Transfer.*|Transfer From.*|Funds? Transfer|..."
```

**Likely bugs:**

- Incomplete coverage: `"FROM NAME"`, `"BY NAME"`, `"SENT TO"`, mixed case leftovers  
- Order of `np.select`: wrong segment chosen before cleanup  
- SBI L131–132 strips account digits but can leave direction residue  
- HDFC `HDFC_CLEAN1` (L106) nukes party if it matches `transfer` / `Amt Trf To`  

---

### 4. Bill transfers with slash-delimited refs (`type/sub-type/numeric/payee`)

**ICICI is the main slash-heavy bill parser** (`ICICI.py` L147–167):

```text
^BIL/INFT/          → sep_by_(..., 2,3) or 4,5 depending on slash count
^BIL/BPAY.*BBPS     → sep_by_(..., 4,5)
^BIL/BPAY|^BIL/RCHG|^BIL/ONL → sep_by_(..., 3,4)
^BIL/00[12].*/.*/NSP0.*/ → 4,5
^BIL/00[12].*/.*/(?!(NSP)) → 2,3 (digits stripped)
^INF/INFT/, ^INF/NEFT/, ^MMT/IMPS, ^RTGS/, ^ACH/, ^GIB/
```

Category: L54 `^BIL/|BPAY/|BBPS` DEBIT → `BILL_PAYMENT`; L64 `BIL/NEFT/` → NEFT.

**Other banks:**

- HDFC L177: payment-gateway cats → `.*/[A-Z]{6}(.*)`  
- HDFC L201: TRANSFER with exactly one `/` → second segment as party  
- PNB L136–138: TRANSFER `^[0-9]{3}/` or `^[0-9]+/` → segment 1  
- IDFC L69–85: IMPS-*/NEFT/RTGS/NACH/UPI slash indices  
- Axis L122, L146–147: UPI/IMPS `sep_by_(...,3,4)`; TRANSFER with 1–2 slashes → segment 0  

**Likely bugs:**

- Fixed slash indices wrong when field order varies (`type/sub-type/numeric/payee` vs `type/payee/numeric`)  
- ICICI L151 strips digits from payee — can destroy alphanumeric names  
- Overlapping rules: same narration matches BILL_PAYMENT and NEFT depending on order  
- `sep_by_` joins slice with `''` (no separator) — multi-segment joins can glue tokens  

---

### 5. Offsetting credits after matching debits: bounce vs reversal

**Adjacent-row heuristics** (`type.shift` / `amount.shift` / `description.shift`):

| File | Lines | Logic |
|---|---|---|
| **HDFC** | 98–99 | CREDIT after DEBIT, same amount: if desc matches **shift(2)** and IMPS\|NEFT\|UPI\|RTGS → **REVERSAL**; if desc matches **shift(1)** → **AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE** |
| **ICICI** | 49–50 | Same amount + same desc as prev DEBIT: IMPS\|NEFT\|UPI\|RTGS → REVERSAL; else → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE |
| **Saraswat** | 20 | Same as ICICI REVERSAL only |
| **StandardCharted** | 60 | Same-amount adjacent + `NACH DR IW` → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE |
| **DCB** | 16 | Adjacent + `^NRTN/CMS` → NEFT_RETURN |

**HDFC-specific bounce subtype** L126:

```python
CHEQUE_PAID (prev) + CHEQUE_RETURN (curr) + prev balance < 0 → INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE
```

**Purpose.py bounce refinement** L145–147:

- `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE` / `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE` from description when category is CHEQUE_RETURN\*  
- Regexes: `RegexConstants.py` L86–87  

**Explicit bounce keywords (examples):**

- HDFC L27: SI/ACH/ECS CREDIT → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE  
- ICICI L18: `REV_NACH` CREDIT → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE  
- Axis L38: `rev_ecs` → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE  

**Likely bugs:**

1. **HDFC L98 uses `description.shift(periods=2)`** for REVERSAL while bounce uses `shift(1)` — off-by-one; reversals may never match or match wrong rows  
2. **ICICI L49–50**: non-rail IMPS/NEFT credits that simply offset a debit (including failed transfers) all become AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE if descriptions match — true payment reversals without rail keywords mislabeled as bounce  
3. **No date window** — only previous row; unsorted statements or intervening rows break matching  
4. **Same description required** — bounce return often has different narration than original debit → misses  
5. Purpose L173 clears subcategory when category contains `BOUNCE|REVERSAL`, which can wipe bounce subtypes set earlier  

---

## Existing tests

**None.** No unit/integration tests, fixtures, or golden narrations in the repo.

---

## Highest-signal bug hotspots (by scenario)

| Scenario | Primary files:lines |
|---|---|
| Cheque / numeric credit | `HDFC.py:69-75,100,188,261`; `Axis.py:58-59`; `PNB.py:60-61`; `IDBI.py:57-58`; `BankRegexConstants.py:80-90` |
| Bare numeric salary | **`HDFC.py:124` (`SAVINGS` typo)**; `Purpose.py:13-17`; `SalaryDetection.py:42-50`; `RegexConstants.py:6-7` |
| Direction words (TO/FROM) | `HDFC.py:253-257`; `Axis.py:167,181`; `ICICI.py:201-203,231-232`; `SBI.py:181` + `TRF_STOP_WORDS`; `UnionBank.py:118-121`; `BankRegexConstants.py:65,140-156,241-298` |
| Slash bill refs | **`ICICI.py:54,64,147-167,228-230`**; `HDFC.py:177,201`; `PNB.py:136-138`; `AppUtil.py:14-15` (`sep_by_`) |
| Bounce vs reversal offset | **`HDFC.py:98-99,126`**; **`ICICI.py:49-50`**; `Purpose.py:145-147,173`; `RegexConstants.py:86-87`; `StandardCharted.py:60`; `Saraswat.py:20` |

---

## Architecture notes for debugging

1. **Bank script runs before Purpose/CleanName** — category mistakes early poison later steps.  
2. **`np.select` first-match** — later more-specific rules never run if an earlier broad rule hits.  
3. **Salary detection needs `partyName`** — empty payee ⇒ no ML salary path.  
4. **CleanName overwrites partyName** with brand names when description/party matches merchant lists — can erase a correctly extracted person name.  
5. **PFM layer** (`PFMCategorization.py` L73–74) collapses anything with REVERSAL\|REFUND\|RETURN\|BOUNCE into PFM `REVERSAL`, and CHEQUE_*/TRANSFER rails into `TRANSFER`.

I can next draft failing test cases or concrete patches for any of the five scenarios.

That matches the adjacent-row bounce rule (L99 in HDFC) rather than the reversal rule (L98).

The reversal rule only triggers when the current row’s description exactly equals the description two rows back (shift(2)). Because the debit is already labelled IMPS/NEFT/UPI/RTGS, the credit’s description is usually something like “IMPS CR-12345” or “UPI-98765”, so it never matches the debit’s description two rows back. The reversal condition therefore fails, and the adjacent-row bounce rule (L99) fires instead.

In other words, the reversal rule is dead for rail transfers because the debit already consumed the early IMPS/NEFT/UPI/RTGS rules.
